title: The DEQ inspector's field form, audited against Cascade
note: Lines and words from spec 12's AUDIT USE section. Every check reads the rows by template_line.

must.line: A1 on file, the permit, expiring November 15, 2026
A2 nothing on file; the renewal was due July 18, 2026 by condition 1.3
A3 on file for 2025, the annual report (case 08)
A5 nothing on file for the September 9, 2026 excursion in the scrubber log
must.corrected: 2026-11-04 (E0a, the owner): added "on_file_gaps" beside nothing_on_file. THE KEY WAS OUT OF DATE, NOT THE ANSWER. The line asks for deviations notified within 24 hours and reported in writing within 15 days. The 2025 annual report ON FILE records the one deviation (S-2 pump failure, August 2025) as reported; what is missing is the notification evidence. That is a document answering the line IN PART, which is exactly what the fifth word is for — and before 4 November there was no word for it, so nothing_on_file was the nearest honest answer and the key froze it. Both pass: a model that still says nothing on file is using the vocabulary this key was written in.

must.line: B1 on file, the scrubber log (case 07), with its missing August week and the September 9 reading
must.corrected: 2026-11-04 (decision 47, E0): added "on_file_gaps". This line's own spec says the document answers it AND names something falling short — the missing August week and the 9 September reading — which is exactly what the fifth word is for. Before the fifth word existed the only honest answer was on_file, so the accept list keeps it: a model that says on_file here is not wrong, it is using the vocabulary it had. Both pass until the whole set has been re-run on the new prompt.
